newsitem.title: USA: US House to vote on CRP extension after 1700 EDT.
newsitem.headline: US House to vote on CRP extension after 1700 EDT.

text.p: The U.S. House will vote after 1700 EDT/2100 GMT Tuesday on a bill allowing a one-year extension of Conservation Reserve contracts, it was announced.
Lawmakers debated the bill for 10 minutes at mid-afternoon. Representative Joe Skeen, R-N.M., demanded a rollcall vote.
Under debate rules for the day, rollcalls could not begin until 1700 EDT.

A two-thirds vote was required to pass the bill, which was brought to the floor on the so-called suspension calendar, normally reserved for noncontroversial bills. No amendments and no more than 40 minutes of debate are allowed on such bills.
"If you want to do right by conservation programs and the environment, vote no on this bill," said Skeen, chairman of the Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture.

Skeen said the bill would block farmers from enrolling fragile land in the Conservation Reserve Program but "it will allow farmers who have highly productive land the opportunity to collect a federal check for one more year."
Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith, sponsor of the bill, described the bill as "a one-time legislative remedy for a problem many of us have seen coming for months."

Smith and cosponsors have said they fear USDA would wait too long in deciding whether to accept farmers' bids to enroll land in the reserve. Farmers could lose up to $600 million in crops if they are not given enough time to prepare fields, he said.
The bill would allow farmers to unilaterally extend their contracts if they notify USDA of the desire.

Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman strongly opposed the bill, which he said would idle productive land at a time when U.S. wheat supplies needed a boost. The bill also would confuse this year's massive turnover of CRP contracts, he said.
Smith modified the bill so it would be void if USDA announced its CRP selections before the bill took effect.
